key_insight: The paper introduces interval and fuzzy physics-augmented neural networks that learn physically constrained lower/mean/upper free-energy branches to quantify and propagate constitutive uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: This gives mechanics engineers a distribution-free way to build hyperelastic models that remain interpretable, data-efficient, and usable in finite element simulations under noisy or sparse stress data.
method: Two-stage transfer learning: fit a sparse mean energy model first, then fine-tune lower and upper branches.
Use automatic differentiation to convert learned free-energy densities into stress predictions.
Embed interval branches into a fuzzy-set representation via alpha-cut interpolation and enforce mechanistic constraints with smoothed L0 regularization.
evidence_signal: On synthetic isotropic hyperelastic data with heteroscedastic noise, shifted noise means, and varying noise magnitudes, the learned bounds enclosed noisy stress observations and generalized to the test set.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful training of the bound branches and constraint/regularization settings, so robustness on real experimental datasets with stronger heterogeneity still needs validation.
paper_title: Interval and fuzzy physics-augmented neural networks (iPANN and fPANN) for uncertainty quantification and propagation in constitutive modeling
